name: Tidal
title: King of Gojim
summary: Tidal was king of Gojim (the nations) and one of the four kings who formed an alliance under the leadership of Kedorlaomer, king of Elam. He participated in the war against the five kings in the Valley of Siddim, where Lot, Abram's nephew, was taken captive. Tidal is mentioned only in connection with this military campaign in Genesis 14.

keyEvents.title: The Alliance of Four Kings
keyEvents.description: Tidal was one of four kings who formed a military alliance under the leadership of Kedorlaomer, king of Elam, to suppress a rebellion among vassal kings in the Jordan Valley.

keyEvents.title: The War Against the Five Kings
keyEvents.description: Tidal and the three other allied kings went to war against the five kings in the Valley of Siddim, including the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah, who had rebelled after twelve years of subjugation.

keyEvents.title: Victory in the Valley of Siddim
keyEvents.description: The four kings, including Chedorlaomer, defeated the five kings in the Valley of Siddim. The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and fell into tar pits in the valley.

keyEvents.title: The Plundering of Sodom and Gomorrah
keyEvents.description: After the victory, Chedorlaomer and his allies plundered Sodom and Gomorrah, taking all their goods and food supplies, and also captured Lot, Abram's nephew.

keyEvents.title: Abram's Counterattack
keyEvents.description: When Abram heard that his nephew Lot had been taken captive, he gathered 318 men and pursued Chedorlaomer and the other kings as far as Dan and then to Hobah, north of Damascus, and defeated them.
